Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital co-lead $30 million expansion to scale Kindo's go-to-market operations and accelerate development of its AI agent management platform
LOS ANGELES , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kindo , the run-anywhere AI agent management platform that puts the enterprise in control, today announced a $30 million raise co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, bringing total capital raised to $57.6 million. The company grew revenue by approximately 800% year over year in 2026 and will use the financing to expand its go-to-market organization and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.
Continue Reading
Meet Kindo video
As autonomous agents spread through the enterprise and their numbers swell into the thousands, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams struggle to control risks and costs without a centralized tool that can discover, observe, and control the entire enterprise AI footprint. Every time a company lets an AI agent access data, update a customer record, approve a request, or change a production system, it delegates authority. The same permissions that let an agent get work done can let it expose sensitive data, make changes outside company policy, disrupt a critical workflow, or rack up huge inference costs.
"Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business," said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo. "What's missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour. That gap is why the teams responsible for supporting and controlling Al are rightfully putting the brakes on Al transformation."
Kindo gives organizations control of the AI agents already running across their operations. It starts with discovery, uncovering shadow AI and mapping where agents are in use, then brings their activity, access, costs, and outcomes into one view. The teams that must support and control AI, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance, get a single set of controls: what employees can do with an agent, what an agent can touch, how it behaves around the clock, and what it costs. The result is an AI Operations Center, SOC- and NOC-style monitoring and intervention for AI, where those teams eliminate risk, drive down cost, and make sure AI delivers measurable outcomes.
Implementation is turnkey and is run by the IT operations staff an organization already has. Teams connect the agents, data sources, and AI models already in use, and from that moment everything is discovered, observed, and controlled from one place. Kindo's gateways govern and audit every call an agent makes to connected data, tools, and approved models. Identity controls apply the organization's existing permissions to people and agents alike, with the option to tighten them centrally. For mission-critical agents that need deeper control, Kindo's harness, purpose-built for centralized agent operations, adds around-the-clock monitoring, support, and direct intervention, including the ability to take over an agent when something goes wrong.

Bay raises $50 million for enterprise AI agent security
Tel Aviv-based Bay has secured $50 million in funding to launch its enterprise AI agent security platform. The platform discovers AI agents and enforces policies at runtime, preventing unintended actions.
TechGig
Published On Nov 13, 2026 at 06:00 AM IST

Highlights
Bay secured $50 million in funding for its enterprise AI agent security platform.
The platform discovers AI agents and enforces policies at runtime.
It prevents unintended actions from prompt injection or agent purpose drift.
Deployment is agentless and takes under five minutes across an entire fleet.
Tel Aviv-based Bay has emerged from stealth with $50 million in funding, comprising a $37 million Series A round led by Battery Ventures and a $13 million seed funding round led by YL Ventures and Striker Venture Partners.
Bay was founded in February 2026 by Yuval Zacharia, Boris Danilovich, and Aner Morag, all alumni of the Israeli Military Intelligence (IDF Unit 8200). The company’s platform provides a single control plane that discovers, understands, and controls AI agents wherever they run within an enterprise.
Upon installation, Bay automatically inventories AI agents, coding assistants, MCP servers, skills, extensions, and local models in use. It also maps their connections, including potentially risky tool combinations.
The platform’s Enforcer component evaluates every proposed agent action in milliseconds within the context of the full session. It decides whether to allow, refer to the user, redirect based on policy, or deny the action.
Bay’s embedded AI system, Lighthouse, automatically builds and maintains policies based on the organisation’s activity history. This system protects against dangerous agent activity, whether caused by malicious prompt injection or organic agent purpose drift.
Bay’s CEO and co-founder Yuval Zacharia told SecurityWeek that effortless deployment, immediate time to value, and clear operationalisation were non-negotiable design principles. The company built a flexible, agentless architecture for deployment across an entire fleet in under five minutes.
Its patented technology retrospectively analyses 30 days of historical logs. This allows customers to see Bay’s potential value and complete a proof of value in less than 14 days. The funding will support product development, engineering team expansion, and go-to-market plans in the US and Europe.

articles.text:
British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 1:09 PM
British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
The British Business Bank has committed an additional £40 million to Harwood Private Capital to increase the availability of flexible financing for smaller and lower-middle-market businesses across the United Kingdom.
The investment supports the first closing of Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II. Commitments to the fund and its related co-investment vehicles now total approximately £120 million.
Harwood will use the capital to provide debt financing for privately held companies pursuing organic expansion, acquisitions, and shareholder transitions. The strategy gives business owners an alternative to conventional bank lending or a complete sale through an M&A transaction.
The commitment increases the British Business Bank’s total investment with Harwood to £75 million. The government-owned development bank previously committed £35 million to the manager’s inaugural HPC UK SME Fund in 2020.
Harwood specializes in flexible private-credit solutions for lower-middle-market companies. Its target borrowers include founder- and family-owned businesses that need additional growth capital but want to preserve ownership and strategic control.
The inaugural fund invested across digital technology, clean-energy supply chains, manufacturing, tourism, and other sectors. One portfolio example is Western Marinas, a Welsh marina operator that used Harwood financing to restore facilities in Wales and southwest England.
That investment supported local jobs and family-operated businesses while attracting visitors and economic activity to surrounding coastal communities. It demonstrates how private credit can finance physical assets and regional companies that may not fit the standardized requirements of traditional lenders.
The British Business Bank’s mandate is to improve access to capital for smaller companies and address financing gaps that can limit growth, productivity, and job creation. In its 2025-2026 financial year, the bank supported £9.4 billion of financing for approximately 38,000 businesses.
That total included £1.3 billion of public funding, £4.3 billion of private capital attracted through the bank’s programs, and £3.7 billion of guaranteed lending. Around 30,000 recipients had not previously received support through the institution.
Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II is intended to extend this impact by supplying customized debt structures for companies whose requirements may not be served adequately by banks or private equity investors.
KEY QUOTES:
“Many smaller businesses continue to face challenges accessing the flexible growth capital they need to scale, invest and realise their ambitions. Harwood has developed a strong track record of providing tailored financing solutions to UK SMEs, particularly those that have not been backed by private equity. Our commitment will help increase the availability of growth capital for businesses, support economic growth and create jobs throughout the UK.”
Adam Kelly, Managing Director of Debt and Regional Funds at the British Business Bank

articles.text:
Orakl Oncology: $34 Million Series A Funding Co-Led By Norrsken VC And Singular To Expand AI-Powered Cancer Drug Discovery
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:56 AM
Orakl Oncology: $34 Million Series A Funding Co-Led By Norrsken VC And Singular To Expand AI-Powered Cancer Drug Discovery
Orakl Oncology, an artificial intelligence-driven biotechnology company developing technologies to improve the prediction of cancer drug responses, has raised $34 million in Series A funding co-led by Norrsken VC and Singular. The financing will support the company’s continued expansion, international hospital partnerships, and development of its AI platform, which combines patient-derived tumor samples, clinical information, and experimental biological data to advance oncology drug research.
The financing was announced by Diane-Laure Pagès, Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of Orakl Oncology, who highlighted the company’s growing network of cancer research partners and expansion plans. The company was founded in 2023 by Pagès, Fanny Jaulin, Ph.D., and Gustave Ronteix.
Orakl originated at Gustave Roussy, the French cancer research and treatment institution where Pagès completed her doctoral studies.
Since its founding, the company has expanded from three co-founders to a team of more than 40 scientists, engineers, AI researchers, and business professionals.
Approximately 30% of its employees hold doctoral degrees.
Orakl plans to establish additional teams in the United States and United Kingdom as it expands its international research and commercial operations.
Building AI Models Around Patient-Derived Cancer Biology
Orakl Oncology is developing an AI platform designed to improve the predictability of responses to cancer treatments.
A central component of its strategy involves generating and analyzing biological information derived from patient tumors.
Cancer treatment responses can vary significantly between patients, even when they have cancers classified within the same disease category.
These differences create challenges for pharmaceutical researchers seeking to identify which experimental medicines are most likely to demonstrate beneficial effects.
Orakl is addressing this problem by combining AI with experimentally generated biological data and associated clinical information.
The company believes training AI systems on information closely connected to actual patient biology can support more relevant drug development research.
Its technology is intended to help researchers understand relationships between tumor characteristics and responses to potential treatments.
Rather than relying exclusively on publicly available datasets, Orakl is building proprietary biological information through its research infrastructure and hospital collaborations.
This approach is designed to provide a foundation for developing AI models focused on oncology drug response prediction.
Expanding International Hospital Partnerships
Orakl has established a network of hospital partnerships supporting access to patient tumor samples and related clinical information.
The company signed five hospital partnerships during 2026.
It also expects more than 15 additional cancer centers across Europe, North America, and Asia to join its network.
These relationships are an important component of Orakl’s approach to developing its AI platform.
Participating hospitals provide research-ready tumor samples and clinical information that can be analyzed alongside laboratory-generated data.
